summary: Built 1939 by the CCC on Dow Butte, staffed until 1982, moved to the Eagle Lake shore in 1994; now a day-use interpretive site.

facts.design: Region 5 cab, one of five cabs of its kind in Region 5 (NHLR)

staffing.status: staffed until 1982 at the original butte; the relocated cab is an interpretive site

access.note: Forest Service: day use only, open sunrise to sunset, no fee; interpretive signage on the southern shore of Eagle Lake

facts.agency: USDA Forest Service, Eagle Lake Ranger District, Lassen National Forest

events.note: Built by the CCC on Dow Butte in the Lassen National Forest
Recalled by a 1971-72 engine crew member: a retired schoolteacher worked the lookout
Removed from the butte and moved to the Eagle Lake shore; sources name the spot Gallatin Marina, Eagle Lake Marina, or the southern shore
Listed on the NHLR on October 15, 1997

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Peakbagging says Gallatin Marina, the blog says Eagle Lake Marina, the 1994 bulletin says the Gallatin area, and the Forest Service says the southern shore of Eagle Lake. The story reports the names and relies on the Forest Service for the current spot.
The register calls the move a restoration at a museum site; the Forest Service calls the cab an interpretive site with signage. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Core facts (1939 build, staffing to 1982, 1994 move, 1997 registration) agree across sources. The record's coordinates (40.55811, -120.78245) sit about 170 m from the Forest Service point (40.557561, -120.780547); the Forest Service point is official and was not changed. Peakbagging gives 6,749 ft for the old butte site while the NHLR gives 6,705 ft; that belongs on the sibling us-ca-dow-butte record, not this one. The 1971-72 staffing recollection is a single account and is dated only to that engine-crew period. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1994 relocation year that the earlier corrections entry proposed is already in events, so the corrections list was cleared. The Forest Service office hours (Tuesday to Friday) are not used in the story; the story points to the office address only.
